match.reason: The closest bank point, Tone and mood, centres on separating the writer's tone from the reader's mood and on naming tone, whereas the new point is about how vocabulary builds mood and shapes style, so it teaches a related but different idea.

draft.title: Word choice and mood
card: Mood is the feeling a passage creates in the reader, such as gloomy, peaceful or tense. Writers build it mainly through the words they choose.
Words carry feelings beyond their basic meaning. "Strolled" and "crept" both mean moved, but "strolled" feels relaxed and "crept" feels secretive.
A group of words with a similar feeling builds one mood. Words such as damp, grey, hollow and silent together build a gloomy mood.
The kinds of words a writer tends to choose over many texts also shape their style, such as plain or ornate, formal or casual.
draft.remember: Words carry feelings, and a group of similar ones builds the mood.

a.q: Which sentence builds a peaceful mood mainly through its word choice?
opts: Soft light drifted over the calm, quiet lake
Cold shadows lurked behind the rotting fence
The siren shrieked as the crowd scrambled away
A single door slammed and everyone froze
a.why: Soft, drifted, calm and quiet all carry a gentle, restful feeling. The other options use words such as lurked, rotting, shrieked and froze, which build gloomy or tense moods.
a.clue: Look for the sentence whose words all feel gentle.

b.q: Priya describes a corridor as narrow and airless, with echoing footsteps behind a girl who clutches her bag. Which mood do these word choices mainly build?
opts: Tense, through words of confinement and pursuit
Peaceful, through words of space and calm
Gloomy, through words of rain and decay
Joyful, through words of movement and light
b.why: Narrow, airless, echoing and clutching suggest confinement and being followed, which builds tension. Gloomy is the most tempting wrong answer, but nothing in the words points to decay or sadness.
b.clue: Ask what the words suggest is happening to her.

a.best: Soft light drifted over the calm, quiet lake

b.best: Tense, through words of confinement and pursuit
